newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM aluminium climbs, helped by LME resilience.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM aluminium climbs, helped by LME resilience.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based aluminium futures ended higher on Thursday, helped by the metal's resilience on the London Metal Exchange (LME), traders said.
"The LME confirmed that support at $1,550 was pretty strong," said one trader. "The outlook is not bad."
The newly listed June contract finished at 185.3 yen per kg, down from 185.5 at the opening.
Other contracts added between 1.0 yen and 1.6 yen after falling to life-of-contract lows on Wednesday.
TOCOM aluminium futures' estimated volume was 2,733 lots.
At 0720 GMT, the benchmark three-month aluminium was quoted at $1,576/78 per tonne, up from the Wednesday afternoon kerb close at $1,569.
In London overnight, aluminium defended its downside, closing down only $8, while copper lost $64.
